Limits: 12 accepted heartbeats per run and 120 per account in a rolling minute, including status changes; 8 KiB heartbeat body. Repeated end requests succeed for a known ID. get.description: Uses the signed-in account's GitHub connection and repository access. Claims remain GitHub comment markers that the CLI reads. A claim must name one of this account's live runs by run ID, chat:run-ID, native harness session, or harness:session; name run explicitly if several live runs match. An exact retry keeps the claim; a concurrent save returns 409. Closed or released issues free the holder's slots on its next claim. PUT claim posts the marker, adds the GitHub viewer as assignee, and moves each project to In Progress. DELETE posts a release marker, removes that assignee, and moves each project to Ready or Todo. Board Done changes status only; it does not close the issue. A GitHub failure can leave an earlier comment, assignee, or project change completed; retry to finish the remaining changes. Missing GitHub access returns 403. List includes other holders but joins run IDs only from this account. Reads inspect at most 1,000 open issue and pull request records, and the latest 1,000 comments per issue, stopping at the latest claim/release marker; longer histories return 422. At most 2,048 saved claims per account; dead run entries expire after 24 hours and unfinished saves after five minutes. Bodies are limited to 8 KiB. Responses are private and no-store.

post.description: Send a message, steer a running turn, stop, or restart through this account's explicitly enabled NIP-HOST binding. The host checks the native operate grant and any calling agent's definition grant. The host resolves the signed native grant through an operator-set caller binding; a request cannot choose its agent identity. Unbound grants refuse. Agent controls default to refused until the shared account-grant checker is installed. The run's computer selects the binding. App chats resolve by run ID or one matching harness session on that host. Other run kinds currently answer not_steerable. Acceptance means the host recorded a command, not that a turn finished. Keep the request ID and command unchanged on retry; changed retries conflict. An unavailable result may have reached the host: retry the same ID. Requests save the exact signed host packet before sending; retries never create a second native operation. At most 4096 command records and 8 MiB per account; records are not evicted. Maximum body 20 KiB. Responses are private and no-store.
